Lena — thanks for the clear asks. Short answers up front, details below and I attached a draft evidence matrix that maps artifacts to the typical auditor requests.

1) Enclave snapshots: we do not hand over full disk images by default. For regulated audits we provide a signed snapshot bundle that includes:
   - KMS-export manifest (HSM-wrapped key metadata)
   - Signed attestation of boot sequence (Timestamps + sig)
   - Container image digests + SBOMs
   - Concise runtime process listing and config tarball

   The bundle is constrained (read-only) and delivered via a secure transfer (S3 presigned link with IP/IAM restrictions) or a NIST FIPS-compliant tape if required by policy. We can also provide an auditor-only staging environment to replay snapshots where cross-references are needed.

2) Fractional evidence model: we support two modes:
   - Rolling snapshot windows: automated 7/30/90-day windows depending on control class; best for continuous controls and forensic log slices.
   - Ad-hoc exports: time-range export for specific UTC timestamps you request (useful for incident-aligned samples).

Operationally, for FedRAMP pre-audit we recommend a 7-day rolling snapshot plus a single ad-hoc export for the auditor-selected time window. That covers sampling for logs and a stable configuration snapshot for control validation.

We attach:
   - evidence_matrix_v2.xlsx (maps controls to artifacts)
   - snapshot_instructions.pdf (how we package and deliver)

Proposed walkthrough: Tue Mar 28 10:00–10:45 PT. Grace, can you join to run through the live demo and the KMS export flow?

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Director, Infrastructure Security
Redwood Inference
